nodes.name: Zn-In/MIL Precursor Formation
nodes.procedure: Zn and In were first coordinated with terephthalic acid to form the Zn-In/MIL precursor. Specifically, a mixture containing 0.18 mmol of BDC, 0.2 mmol of Zn(NO3)2·6H2O, and 0.2 mmol of In(NO3)3·6H2O and 10 mL of DMF was prepared in a 100 mL round bottom flask. The mixture was subjected to ultrasonication for 30 min to ensure uniform dispersion of the components. Subsequently, the flask was heated in an oil bath at 130°C for 1 h, during which a white precipitate formed. The precipitate was then isolated by centrifugation, washed thoroughly, and dried.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Defect-Rich Conductive Carbon Rods: Initially, a mixture containing 0.18 mmol of BDC... dried.

nodes.name: Carbonization and Acid Etching
nodes.procedure: Next, the collected precipitate was heated to 950°C under nitrogen atmosphere at a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹ and maintained at this temperature for 3 h. Following this, the pyrolyzed powder was treated with 3 M nitric acid for 1 h at 50°C. The treated powder was washed by centrifugation several times and then dried under vacuum to obtain the defective conductive carbon rod.

nodes.source_text: Next, the collected precipitate was heated to 950°C under nitrogen atmosphere... dried under vacuum to obtain the defective conductive carbon rod.

nodes.name: Impregnation and Reduction
nodes.procedure: 0.05 mmol of Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, 0.1 mmol of RuCl3·H2O and 20 mL of deionized water were placed in a 50 mL round-bottomed flask and ultrasonicated for 30 min to disperse them evenly. Next, 100 mg of defect-rich conductive carbon rod was added to the flask and sonicated again to achieve uniform distribution. The flask was then immersed in an oil bath at 100°C, allowing the solution to evaporate completely and yielding a black powder. The black powder was transferred to a tube furnace, where it was heated to 500°C at a ramp rate of 5°C min⁻¹ under a H2/Ar atmosphere (10% H2 90% Ar) for 2 h. Finally, the product was cooled to room temperature, resulting in the formation of the RuNC·O·CeSA/C electrocatalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show uniform distribution of Ru clusters on carbon support with average particle size of 1.3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of Ru_NC -O- Ce_SA / C electrocatalyst exhibit a uniform distribution of Ru clusters on the surface of the carbon carriers, with an average particle size of 1.3 nm (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.235, 0.214, and 0.205 nm corresponding to (100), (002), and (101) planes of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images elucidate the lattice stripes of Ru, with spacings of 0.235, 0.214, and 0.205 nm, corresponding to the (100), (002), and (101) crystalline planes of Ru, respectively (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM confirms coexistence of Ru clusters and Ce single atoms on carbon carriers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) images confirm the coexistence of Ru clusters with Ce single atoms on the carbon carriers (Figure 1d,e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of C, O, Ru, and Ce elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping images further demonstrate that the elements of C, O, Ru, and Ce are uniformly distributed on the carbon carriers.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows broad C (002) peak at 25° and Ru peaks at 38°, 42°, 44° for (100), (002), (101) planes; no rare earth crystal peaks detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of the Ru_NC - O - Ce_SA / C electrocatalysts is revealed through X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns. A broad peak, attributed to the (002) plane of C, is evident at 25°C ... three distinct peaks are visible near 38°, 42°, and 44° corresponding to the (100) and (002) and (101) planes of Ru (Figure 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET analysis shows specific surface area of 1499.6 m² g⁻¹ and average pore size of 3.7 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru_NC -O- Ce_SA / C electrocatalyst shows a specific surface area of 1499.6 m² g⁻¹ and an average pore size of 3.7 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3d XPS shows coexistence of Ru⁰ and Ruⁿ⁺ with peaks shifted to higher binding energies relative to Ru/C; Ce 3d XPS shows Ce³⁺ peaks at 885.08 and 902.21 eV and Ce⁴⁺ peaks; O 1s XPS shows 16.2% metallic oxygen indicating M-O bonds formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Ru 3d spectra, Ru_NC -O- Ce_SA/C shows the coexistence of Ru⁰ and Ruⁿ⁺ (Figure 2b). Both the Ru⁰ 3d_{2/5} and Ruⁿ⁺ 3d_{2/5} peaks of Ru_NC -O- Ce_SA/C are shifted to higher binding energies relative to those of Ru/C ... The O 1s spectrum of Ru_NC -O- Ce_SA/C is shown in Figure 2d, with 16.2% of metallic oxygen, indicating the formation of M-O bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function of 4.43 eV for Ru_NC -O- Ce_SA / C, indicating electron transfer from Ru to Ce.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated Φ value of Ru/C is 4.39 eV, lower than that of Ce_SA / C (4.50 eV). After the formation of Ru_NC -O- Ce_SA / C, its work function is 4.43 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows average Ru valence between 0 and +4; Ce L₃-edge shows predominant Ce³⁺ valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru K-edge Xray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra demonstrate that the edge absorption energy of Ru_NC -O- Ce_SA / C is intermediate between those of the Ru foils and RuO₂ ... The valence state of Ce in Ru_NC - O - Ce_SA / C is also characterized by the XANES spectrum ... the predominant valence state of Ce is +3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ru-O at 1.55 Å and Ru-Ru at 2.35 Å; Ce L₃-edge shows Ce-O at 2.00 Å, no Ce-Ce peak confirming single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ru K-edge Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra, the two peaks observed at 1.55 and 2.35 Å in Ru_NC - O - Ce_SA / C are assigned to Ru-O (Ruⁿ⁺ sites) and Ru-Ru (Ru⁰ sites) bonds, respectively ... a distinct peak at 2.00 Å corresponding to Ce-O coordination is observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Ru-H peaks at 1820 cm⁻¹ (Ru⁰) and 1960 cm⁻¹ (Ruⁿ⁺), Ru-O at 515 cm⁻¹, OH bending on Ru⁰ at 715 cm⁻¹, confirming coexistence of Ru⁰ and Ruⁿ⁺ sites with stable Ruⁿ⁺-O band across HER/HOR potentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra reveals several key features: the characteristic peak at 1820 cm⁻¹ is attributed to the vibration of the Ru-H bond associated with adsorbed hydrogen (H_ad) on the metallic Ru⁰ surfaces. The Raman signature peak near 1960 cm⁻¹ is indicative of the Ru-H bond vibrations formed between the adsorbed hydrogen species and high-valent Ruⁿ⁺ surface.
